GPS data processing pipeline

MTL Explorer uses Kalman smoothing by default. The canonical stream contains estimates and explicit support decisions; a smooth path does not prove that the source positions were correct.

On this page
  • Import and estimation
  • Interval contract
  • Background batches
  • Storage and consumers
  • Review and validation
  • Source diagnosis and timing provenance
  • Indexer queue and recovery

Import and estimation

Background source assessment and import use the configurable GPSBabel allowance mtl.indexer.gps.conversion-timeout (default PT10M). Interactive review/export use their separate one-minute limit. Both conversion modes produce the same GPX content and preserve the original source; cancellation still terminates the converter. Native GPX and Java GeoJSON parsing do not use this subprocess limit.

GPSBabel conversions, including review previews and import fallbacks, run outside database transactions. A source lock spans preparation and saving; diagnosis commits separately, then imported tracks and replacement changes commit atomically. Source revisions are checked before saving, and import failures are recorded after rollback.

  1. FIT and other supported formats are converted upstream; GPXReader parses GPX observations with fractional timestamps, source section identity, and available fix, satellite, HDOP, VDOP, speed and source metadata.
  2. RAW preserves parsed coordinates, including missing altitude/time and rejected 0,0 fixes. It is an observation trace, not a byte-level copy of the original file. Missing altitude and time serialize as JSON null.
  3. Horizontal plausibility and probation reject short excursions. Probation uses the longer of its positive entry interval and the interval since the previous probation observation, with the usual 120-second time-credit cap. It does not accumulate time across a suspect cluster. This preserves strict checks for fast loggers while allowing recovery after near-duplicate fixes when normal observation spacing resumes. Equal, backward and missing entry timestamps retain their existing plausibility rules. A stable relocated cluster starts a disconnected recording span. Recording segments, clock resets and gaps over 120 seconds also break continuity.
  4. ElevationObservationFilter rejects short, bounded vertical excursions independently of horizontal movement. Rejected altitude stays unknown. Persistent altitude steps remain reviewable rather than being removed on an unsupported assumption.
  5. BreakStopTreatment removes isolated position spikes. It no longer detects stops or collapses stationary observations into anchor pairs.
  6. Startup altitude stabilization and Kalman/RTS smoothing operate within recording spans. The transition and process noise use each actual time step; missing measurements skip the update. Source quality and large innovations increase measurement uncertainty.
  7. RAW_OUTLIER_CLEANED stores the full-density canonical result. TrackMotionAnalyzer then classifies moving, stopped, and unknown intervals without changing accepted coordinates or elevation. Point metrics, duration, chart windows, peaks, energy, and events consume the stored support and motion decisions. See motion analysis.

The Kalman settings are under mtl.denoise. Defaults are horizontal/vertical measurement sigmas 6/10 m and horizontal/vertical acceleration sigmas 2/0.5 m/s². The constructor fallback is also Kalman. Median remains an explicit option. Processing evidence records the selected algorithm, pipeline identifier and Kalman parameters. DOP changes relative uncertainty; it is not an error radius.

Interval contract

A point's intervalStatus describes the interval from the preceding point.

Status Meaning Metric support
START First point No preceding interval.
OBSERVED Positive, continuous timed observations Distance/time; altitude-derived metrics require valid altitude.
STOPPED Stationary anchor support retained by the interval model Supported elapsed time. Current imports classify stops separately with motionState; they do not create collapsed anchor pairs.
GEOMETRY_ONLY Nearby observations without usable elapsed time Geometry distance; no speed, power or energy estimate.
UNKNOWN Recording break or unsupported connection No connecting distance, ascent, speed or energy estimate. Positive elapsed time contributes to unknown duration.

Geometry-only support is bounded to 200 m without time, or 5 m for equal timestamps. Backward time never establishes a connecting edge. Motion inference uses a separate, stricter 60-second observation-gap limit. Moving, confirmed stopped and unknown seconds partition a complete increasing timeline. Missing time and backward clock resets cannot establish an absolute duration; their unknown length must not be interpreted as measured zero time.

Missing altitude resets the vertical baseline. A shared 2 m ascent/descent gate feeds cumulative climbing, vertical rates and gravitational energy. Unsupported rates and peaks are null. Power limits also cap the accumulated energy and record energyLimited, so a plausible chart cannot hide an unbounded total. Energy remains an activity-dependent mechanical estimate calculated after classification.

Background batches

Energy, duplicate detection, activity classification, exploration, photo correlation, exercise-route association and synthetic demo health process bounded batches. A full batch with progress schedules its next batch immediately through the existing scheduler. Each callback yields its scheduler thread before the next batch; one running flag per job prevents overlap and duplicate continuation chains.

Temporary DB connection acquisition failures pause duplicate/classification batches before marking a track failed. The current and later tracks remain pending and retry on the existing periodic schedule. Authentication, configuration and data errors are distinguished from temporary connection failures.

Idle or failed batches stop their continuation and retry on the existing periodic schedule. Energy and demo-health idle checks default to five seconds. Energy generations, delayed energy/media retries, indexing prerequisites and the shared heavy-job guard remain in their respective workers. Exploration failures wait for its normal retry rather than immediately recalculating the same failed batch. Exercise associations commit metadata, activity changes and energy requests together before another batch runs.

Shutdown checks stop new batches and leave pending records for restart. File indexers already use worker queues; remote sync, downloads and service probes keep their own schedules and limits.

Storage and consumers

Variant Consumers
RAW Quality review and audit.
RAW_OUTLIER_CLEANED Authoritative point metrics, server chart buckets, energy and crossing analysis.
SIMPLIFIED_SHAPE Map rendering at 1, 10, 100 and 1000 m; points refer back to canonical indices.

recordingBreakBeforePointIndexes preserves both ends of discontinuities through simplification and map rendering. observed_path is a separate XY MultiLineString used by proximity, photo-route matching and exploration queries; it omits connecting gap edges. Coordinate arrays retain their stable point indices. Photo position interpolation requires an observed adjacent interval or an exact observation. Disconnected tracks are excluded from automatic Frechet matching, which assumes one continuous curve. Custom SQL written against the flat track column must use observed_path when continuity matters.

Track Details charts use server buckets over canonical points, not map simplification. Main maps, point layers, the Details minimap and the GPS review map preserve recording breaks. Single-track 3D replay is unavailable across recording gaps. Crossing analysis also splits recording spans before timing.

Review and validation

Track Details → Quality → Review GPS observations loads GET /api/tracks/{trackId}/quality on demand. Original and processed paths can be toggled; selecting a review item shows its location, source evidence and possible metric impact. Reasons include rejected observations, large corrections, stationary support, unknown intervals and limited energy. The list shows up to 250 items, ranked by a heuristic impact score, not calibrated confidence.

See the pipeline reliability tests and source assessment tests. Synthetic cases cover known failures and numerical consistency. Correlated GPS drift, slow movement and altitude steps can still be ambiguous. Ground-truth field evaluation is needed before claiming universal accuracy improvements.

New derived fields are populated by new imports. Existing databases must be recreated/reimported to obtain complete evidence and observed paths; no legacy backfill is included in those field changes. Changeset 082 separately schedules one ordinary GPS reimport; see release upgrade instructions.

Source diagnosis and timing provenance

Source review assesses recorded evidence and processing results independently of repair. Severe timing findings are contained before temporal splitting; original timestamps remain in RAW observations. Estimated repairs retain their provenance on reimport. Untimed GPX routes can supply geometry without measured duration, speed, energy, or time-based health/photo matching.

Findings mark a source as needing review; they do not automatically exclude it from the map or statistics. Saved use decisions control those exclusions. Estimated, conflicting, or otherwise unsupported timing independently restricts time-based calculations, duplicate preference, and exploration eligibility. Including a source does not convert estimated timing into measurements. See source review and the GPS quality module boundary.

Indexer queue and recovery

New and changed files become pending as soon as discovery is committed, even while imports are waiting. Processing shows Discovering while the file total is still growing, then reports progress against the committed queue. GPS and media counts describe source files, not track points or tracks inside a file.

Manual rescans retry failed files even when their size and modification time are unchanged. Startup and scheduled scans recover pending work and changed files without repeatedly importing unchanged failed sources. Stable zero-byte GPS and media files are informational Skipped outcomes and are processed when their contents change. Earlier imported data stays available and is identified as retained data.

Incomplete storage scans preserve imported database records. Removal stays pending until database cleanup succeeds; failures retain their operation and error. The indexer never deletes original GPS or media files. Completion writes retry temporary database failures, and a rescan can recover pending work whose worker is no longer active.

When duplicate detection or activity classification cannot temporarily obtain a database connection, the batch pauses and leaves its tracks pending for the next scheduled turn. Invalid data and permanent errors keep their failure diagnostics. This retry does not increase worker threads or the database pool size.

New derived fields are calculated by normal imports; legacy backfill is not the default policy. Acknowledgement semantics are described in source issues.
